biography.plain_text: Pierre Titley was a Canadian real estate entrepreneur who established RE/MAX in Quebec and developed its provincial brokerage network. He also owned the group's New York regional franchise, which he sold while retaining the Quebec business. His work helped independent agents compete through a model offering them a larger share of commissions.

long_biography.plain_text:
As the founder of RE/MAX Quebec, Pierre Titley helped reshape the professional standing of its brokers. He lobbied for their recognition as self-employed workers, while his company introduced Tranquilli-T, a programme offering sellers protection against specified problems and legal assistance after a property sale.

Titley also initiated the network's partnership with Opération Enfant Soleil, which supported paediatric care across Quebec. Brokers and office teams raised funds through golf tournaments, benefit dinners and sporting challenges. During the telethon, agencies became telephone centres to receive public donations. Titley joined colleagues to present the network's collective contribution, which combined money raised by brokers, their families and the wider public.

Primary retained ownership in Quebec after the New York disposal and serving founder role at death jointly support terminal principal-core continuity. Company history distinguishes 1981 introduction from the first office in May 1982. Primary charitable descriptions refer variously to the first 1987 telethon and 1988 partnership; biographies omit this date discrepancy.

Complete relevant primary releases, history, court passage, monitor ownership section, obituary body and industry profiles were read. The original investor-relations URL now redirects, but the unchanged issuer release was recovered in full on PR Newswire. No legal allegation enters the published biographies.

Corporate market share, franchise agents' property turnover and collective charity proceeds are not Titley's personal wealth or individual donations. The short commission benefit follows the directly reported model, not an invented personal motive.
